record.context_brief: Newton inequalities for stable GKK τ-matrices
record.original_question: If A is a stable GKK τ-matrix, meaning that A is both GKK and τ and all eigenvalues of A lie in the open right half-plane, must A satisfy the Newton inequalities c_j^2 ≥ c_{j-1} c_{j+1} for every j = 1,…,n−1, where c_j = (∑_{#α=j} A[α]) / (n choose j)?

evidence.quote: A matrix is called positive stable if its spectrum lies entirely in the open right half plane. In the se quel, we will shorten the term ‘positive stable’ to simply ‘stable’.
5. Newton’s inequalities. For a matrix A, let cj := ∑ #α=j A[α]/ ( n j ) , j = 0, . . . , n.
This problem has possible subproblems, e.g., 5b. Newton’s inequalities for stable GKK τ -matrices.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A=(a_{ij})$ be an $n\times n$ real matrix. For an index set $\alpha\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$, denote by $A[\alpha]$ the principal minor of $A$ corresponding to rows and columns indexed by $\alpha$, and let $|\alpha|$ denote the cardinality of $\alpha$. Define the normalized principal minor sums
$$c_j(A) \;=\; \frac{1}{\binom{n}{j}}\sum_{|\alpha|=j} A[\alpha], \qquad j=0,1,\dots,n,$$
with the convention $c_0(A)=1$.

Recall the following definitions:
- $A$ is called a $\tau$-matrix if for every nonempty index set $\alpha\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$ and every $i\in\alpha$, one has $A[\alpha]\cdot A[\alpha\setminus\{i\}\cup\{i\}] \ge$ (the usual $\tau$ inequality between adjacent principal minors holds); equivalently, $A$ satisfies all the $\tau$-inequalities relating principal minors indexed by sets differing by one element in the standard way.
- $A$ is called a GKK matrix (Gantmacher–Krein–Koteljanskii) if every principal minor of $A$ is positive and $A$ satisfies the Koteljanskii (Hadamard–Fischer type) inequalities $A[\alpha\cup\beta]\,A[\alpha\cap\beta] \le A[\alpha]\,A[\beta]$ for all index sets $\alpha,\beta\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$.
- $A$ is called (positive) stable if every eigenvalue of $A$ lies in the open right half-plane $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Re}(z)>0\}$.

Question: Suppose $A$ is an $n\times n$ matrix that is simultaneously GKK, $\tau$, and (positive) stable. Must $A$ satisfy Newton's inequalities
$$c_j(A)^2 \;\ge\; c_{j-1}(A)\,c_{j+1}(A) \qquad \text{for every } j=1,\dots,n-1\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: A search located the source listing this as an open subproblem (Newton's inequalities for stable GKK τ-matrices) but did not surface any subsequent publication resolving it. Related work shows that not all GKK τ-matrices are stable, but the Newton-inequality question for the stable subclass appears unresolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on GKK tau-matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems on GKK τ-matrices, including Newton's inequalities as a listed subproblem.
status_evidence.claim: The Newton-inequality question for stable GKK τ-matrices is posed as an open subproblem.

status_evidence.title: Not all GKK τ-matrices are stable
status_evidence.snippet: Examples of GKK τ-matrices that fail to be stable are constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Stability of GKK τ-matrices is known to fail in general, but the Newton-inequality consequence for the stable case is not addressed.
